title: A simple way to break a bad habit
speaker: Judson Brewer

sentences.en: When I was first learning to meditate, the instruction was to simply pay attention to my breath, and when my mind wandered, to bring it back.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次学习冥想时，指导是简单地注意我的呼吸，当我的思绪走神时，将其拉回来。

sentences.en: Sounded simple enough. Yet I'd sit on these silent retreats, sweating through T-shirts in the middle of winter.
sentences.zh: 听起来很简单。然而，在隆冬，我会坐在这些安静的休息处，汗流浃背地穿着T恤。

sentences.en: I'd take naps every chance I got because it was really hard work.
sentences.zh: 我一有机会就会小睡一下，因为这真的很辛苦。

sentences.en: Actually, it was exhausting. The instruction was simple enough but I was missing something really important.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那是很累的。说明很简单，但我遗漏了一些非常重要的东西。

sentences.en: So why is it so hard to pay attention? Well, studies show that even when we're really trying to pay attention to something -- like maybe this talk -- at some point, about half of us will drift off into a daydream,
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这么难引起注意呢？嗯，研究表明，即使我们真的很想注意某件事——比如这次演讲——在某些时候，大约一半的人会陷入白日梦，

sentences.en: or have this urge to check our Twitter feed.
sentences.zh: 或者有查看我们的 Twitter 消息的冲动。

sentences.en: So what's going on here? It turns out that we're fighting one of the most evolutionarily-conserved learning processes currently known in science, one that's conserved back to the most basic nervous systems known to man.
sentences.zh: 那么这是怎么回事呢？事实证明，我们正在对抗目前科学界已知的进化上最保守的学习过程之一，这种学习过程可以追溯到人类已知的最基本的神经系统。

sentences.en: This reward-based learning process is called positive and negative reinforcement, and basically goes like this.
sentences.zh: 这种基于奖励的学习过程称为正强化和负强化，基本上是这样的。

sentences.en: We see some food that looks good, our brain says, "Calories! ... Survival!"
sentences.zh: 我们看到一些看起来不错的食物，我们的大脑会说：“卡路里！……生存！”

sentences.en: We eat the food, we taste it -- it tastes good.
sentences.zh: 我们吃食物，我们品尝它——味道很好。

sentences.en: And especially with sugar, our bodies send a signal to our brain that says, "Remember what you're eating and where you found it."
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于糖，我们的身体会向大脑发送信号：“记住你在吃什么以及在哪里找到它。”

sentences.en: We lay down this context-dependent memory and learn to repeat the process next time.
sentences.zh: 我们放下这种与情境相关的记忆，并学习下次重复这个过程。

sentences.en: See food, eat food, feel good, repeat. Trigger, behavior, reward.
sentences.zh: 看到食物，吃食物，感觉良好，重复。触发因素、行为、奖励。

sentences.en: Simple, right? Well, after a while, our creative brains say, "You know what?
sentences.zh: 很简单，对吧？好吧，过了一会儿，我们的创造性大脑会说：“你知道吗？

sentences.en: You can use this for more than just remembering where food is.
sentences.zh: 您不仅可以使用它来记住食物在哪里。

sentences.en: You know, next time you feel bad, why don't you try eating something good so you'll feel better?"
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，下次你感觉不好的时候，为什么不尝试吃点好东西，这样你就会感觉好点呢？”

sentences.en: We thank our brains for the great idea, try this and quickly learn that if we eat chocolate or ice cream when we're mad or sad, we feel better.
sentences.zh: 我们感谢我们的大脑提供了这个好主意，尝试一下，很快就会发现，如果我们在生气或悲伤时吃巧克力或冰淇淋，我们会感觉更好。

sentences.en: Same process, just a different trigger. Instead of this hunger signal coming from our stomach, this emotional signal -- feeling sad -- triggers that urge to eat.
sentences.zh: 相同的过程，只是不同的触发器。这种饥饿信号不是来自我们的胃，而是这种情感信号——感到悲伤——触发了吃东西的冲动。

sentences.en: Maybe in our teenage years, we were a nerd at school, and we see those rebel kids outside smoking and we think, "Hey, I want to be cool."
sentences.zh: 也许在我们十几岁的时候，我们在学校是个书呆子，当我们看到那些叛逆的孩子在外面抽烟时，我们会想，“嘿，我想变得很酷。”

sentences.en: So we start smoking. The Marlboro Man wasn't a dork, and that was no accident.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始吸烟。万宝路男人不是个傻瓜，这也不是偶然的。

sentences.en: See cool, smoke to be cool, feel good. Repeat.
sentences.zh: 看得爽，抽得爽，心情好。重复。

sentences.en: Trigger, behavior, reward. And each time we do this, we learn to repeat the process and it becomes a habit.
sentences.zh: 触发因素、行为、奖励。每次我们这样做时，我们都会学会重复这个过程，并成为一种习惯。

sentences.en: So later, feeling stressed out triggers that urge to smoke a cigarette or to eat something sweet.
sentences.zh: 所以后来，感到压力会引发吸烟或吃甜食的冲动。

sentences.en: Now, with these same brain processes, we've gone from learning to survive to literally killing ourselves with these habits.
sentences.zh: 现在，通过这些相同的大脑过程，我们已经从学习生存变成了用这些习惯自杀。

sentences.en: Obesity and smoking are among the leading preventable causes of morbidity and mortality in the world.
sentences.zh: 肥胖和吸烟是世界上发病率和死亡率的主要可预防原因之一。

sentences.en: So back to my breath. What if instead of fighting our brains, or trying to force ourselves to pay attention, we instead tapped into this natural, reward-based learning process ...
sentences.zh: 回到我的呼吸。如果我们不再与我们的大脑作斗争，或者试图强迫自己集中注意力，而是利用这种自然的、基于奖励的学习过程，会怎么样……

sentences.en: but added a twist? What if instead we just got really curious about what was happening in our momentary experience?
sentences.zh: 但添加了一个转折？如果我们只是对我们短暂的经历中发生的事情感到非常好奇怎么办？

sentences.en: I'll give you an example. In my lab, we studied whether mindfulness training could help people quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。在我的实验室里，我们研究了正念训练是否可以帮助人们戒烟。

sentences.en: Now, just like trying to force myself to pay attention to my breath, they could try to force themselves to quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 现在，就像试图强迫自己注意呼吸一样，他们可以尝试强迫自己戒烟。

sentences.en: And the majority of them had tried this before and failed -- on average, six times.
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数人以前都尝试过这种方法，但都失败了——平均六次。

sentences.en: Now, with mindfulness training, we dropped the bit about forcing and instead focused on being curious.
sentences.zh: 现在，通过正念训练，我们放弃了强迫，而是专注于保持好奇心。

sentences.en: In fact, we even told them to smoke. What? Yeah, we said, "Go ahead and smoke, just be really curious about what it's like when you do."
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们甚至告诉他们抽烟。什么？是的，我们说，“抽烟吧，只是对抽烟时的感觉感到好奇。”

sentences.en: And what did they notice? Well here's an example from one of our smokers.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到了什么？这是我们一位吸烟者的例子。

sentences.en: She said, "Mindful smoking: smells like stinky cheese and tastes like chemicals, YUCK!"
sentences.zh: 她说：“正念吸烟：闻起来像臭奶酪，尝起来像化学品，恶心！”

sentences.en: Now, she knew, cognitively that smoking was bad for her, that's why she joined our program.
sentences.zh: 现在，她从认知上知道吸烟对她有害，这就是她加入我们项目的原因。

sentences.en: What she discovered just by being curiously aware when she smoked was that smoking tastes like shit.
sentences.zh: 当她吸烟时，她好奇地意识到，吸烟的味道就像屎一样。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, she moved from knowledge to wisdom.
sentences.zh: （笑声）现在，她从知识走向了智慧。

sentences.en: She moved from knowing in her head that smoking was bad for her to knowing it in her bones, and the spell of smoking was broken.
sentences.zh: 她从头脑里知道吸烟对她不好，变成了深入骨髓，吸烟的魔咒被打破了。

sentences.en: She started to become disenchanted with her behavior.
sentences.zh: 她开始对自己的行为不再抱有幻想。

sentences.en: Now, the prefrontal cortex, that youngest part of our brain from an evolutionary perspective, it understands on an intellectual level that we shouldn't smoke.
sentences.zh: 现在，从进化的角度来看，前额叶皮层是我们大脑中最年轻的部分，它在智力层面上理解我们不应该吸烟。

sentences.en: And it tries its hardest to help us change our behavior, to help us stop smoking, to help us stop eating that second, that third, that fourth cookie.
sentences.zh: 它尽最大努力帮助我们改变行为，帮助我们戒烟，帮助我们停止吃第二块、第三块、第四块饼干。

sentences.en: We call this cognitive control. We're using cognition to control our behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为认知控制。我们正在利用认知来控制我们的行为。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, this is also the first part of our brain that goes offline when we get stressed out, which isn't that helpful.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，当我们感到压力时，这也是我们大脑第一个离线的部分，这并没有多大帮助。

sentences.en: Now, we can all relate to this in our own experience.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们都可以从自己的经历中体会到这一点。

sentences.en: We're much more likely to do things like yell at our spouse or kids when we're stressed out or tired, even though we know it's not going to be helpful.
sentences.zh: 当我们感到压力或疲倦时，我们更有可能做一些事情，比如对配偶或孩子大喊大叫，即使我们知道这不会有帮助。

sentences.en: We just can't help ourselves. When the prefrontal cortex goes offline, we fall back into our old habits, which is why this disenchantment is so important.
sentences.zh: 我们只是无法帮助自己。当前额叶皮层离线时，我们就会回到原来的习惯，这就是为什么这种祛魅如此重要的原因。

sentences.en: Seeing what we get from our habits helps us understand them at a deeper level -- to know it in our bones so we don't have to force ourselves to hold back or restrain ourselves from behavior.
sentences.zh: 了解我们从习惯中得到什么有助于我们更深入地理解它们——从骨子里了解它，这样我们就不必强迫自己克制自己的行为。

sentences.en: We're just less interested in doing it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们只是一开始就不太感兴趣这样做。

sentences.en: And this is what mindfulness is all about: Seeing really clearly what we get when we get caught up in our behaviors, becoming disenchanted on a visceral level and from this disenchanted stance, naturally letting go.
sentences.zh: 这就是正念的意义所在：真正清楚地看到当我们陷入自己的行为中时我们会得到什么，在内心层面上变得不再抱有幻想，并从这种不再抱有幻想的立场中自然地放手。

sentences.en: This isn't to say that, poof, magically we quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说，噗，我们神奇地戒烟了。

sentences.en: But over time, as we learn to see more and more clearly the results of our actions, we let go of old habits and form new ones.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，当我们越来越清楚地看到我们行为的结果时，我们就会放弃旧习惯并形成新习惯。

sentences.en: The paradox here is that mindfulness is just about being really interested in getting close and personal with what's actually happening in our bodies and minds from moment to moment.
sentences.zh: 这里的悖论是，正念只是真正有兴趣接近和个人了解我们身体和思想中每时每刻实际发生的事情。

sentences.en: This willingness to turn toward our experience rather than trying to make unpleasant cravings go away as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 这种愿意转向我们的经验而不是试图让不愉快的渴望尽快消失的意愿。

sentences.en: And this willingness to turn toward our experience is supported by curiosity, which is naturally rewarding.
sentences.zh: 这种转向我们的经验的意愿是由好奇心支持的，这自然是有益的。

sentences.en: What does curiosity feel like? It feels good.
sentences.zh: 好奇心是什么感觉？感觉很好。

sentences.en: And what happens when we get curious? We start to notice that cravings are simply made up of body sensations -- oh, there's tightness, there's tension, there's restlessness -- and that these body sensations come and go.
sentences.zh: 当我们好奇时会发生什么？我们开始注意到，渴望只是由身体感觉组成的——哦，有紧绷、有紧张、有不安——而且这些身体感觉来来去去。

sentences.en: These are bite-size pieces of experiences that we can manage from moment to moment rather than getting clobbered by this huge, scary craving that we choke on.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们可以时时刻刻管理的小片段体验，而不是被我们窒息的巨大而可怕的渴望所破坏。

sentences.en: In other words, when we get curious, we step out of our old, fear-based, reactive habit patterns, and we step into being.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当我们感到好奇时，我们就会摆脱旧有的、基于恐惧的、反应性的习惯模式，并步入存在。

sentences.en: We become this inner scientist where we're eagerly awaiting that next data point.
sentences.zh: 我们成为了一位内心的科学家，热切地等待着下一个数据点。

sentences.en: Now, this might sound too simplistic to affect behavior.
sentences.zh: 现在，这听起来可能太简单了，无法影响行为。

sentences.en: But in one study, we found that mindfulness training was twice as good as gold standard therapy at helping people quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 但在一项研究中，我们发现正念训练在帮助人们戒烟方面的效果是黄金标准疗法的两倍。

sentences.en: So it actually works. And when we studied the brains of experienced meditators, we found that parts of a neural network of self-referential processing called the default mode network were at play.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实有效。当我们研究经验丰富的冥想者的大脑时，我们发现称为默认模式网络的自我参照处理神经网络的一部分正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: Now, one current hypothesis is that a region of this network, called the posterior cingulate cortex, is activated not necessarily by craving itself but when we get caught up in it, when we get sucked in, and it takes us for a ride.
sentences.zh: 现在，目前的一个假设是，这个网络的一个区域，称为后扣带皮层，不一定是由渴望本身激活的，而是当我们陷入其中时，当我们被吸进去时，它会带我们去兜风。

sentences.en: In contrast, when we let go -- step out of the process just by being curiously aware of what's happening -- this same brain region quiets down.
sentences.zh: 相反，当我们放手时——仅仅通过好奇地意识到正在发生的事情来退出这个过程——同一大脑区域就会安静下来。

sentences.en: Now we're testing app and online-based mindfulness training programs that target these core mechanisms and, ironically, use the same technology that's driving us to distraction to help us step out of our unhealthy habit patterns
sentences.zh: 现在，我们正在测试针对这些核心机制的应用程序和基于在线的正念训练计划，具有讽刺意味的是，使用使我们分心的相同技术来帮助我们摆脱不健康的习惯模式

sentences.en: of smoking, of stress eating and other addictive behaviors.
sentences.zh: 吸烟、压力饮食和其他成瘾行为。

sentences.en: Now, remember that bit about context-dependent memory?
sentences.zh: 现在，还记得上下文相关记忆吗？

sentences.en: We can deliver these tools to peoples' fingertips in the contexts that matter most.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在最重要的环境中将这些工具交付给人们。

sentences.en: So we can help them tap into their inherent capacity to be curiously aware right when that urge to smoke or stress eat or whatever arises.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以帮助他们利用其固有的能力，在出现吸烟或压力饮食或其他任何情况时好奇地意识到这一点。

sentences.en: So if you don't smoke or stress eat, maybe the next time you feel this urge to check your email when you're bored, or you're trying to distract yourself from work, or maybe to compulsively respond to that text message when you're driving,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您不吸烟或压力饮食，也许下次您感到无聊时查看电子邮件的冲动，或者您试图分散自己的工作注意力，或者可能在开车时强迫性地回复短信时，

sentences.en: see if you can tap into this natural capacity, just be curiously aware of what's happening in your body and mind in that moment.
sentences.zh: 看看你是否可以利用这种自然能力，只是好奇地意识到那一刻你的身体和心灵正在发生什么。

sentences.en: It will just be another chance to perpetuate one of our endless and exhaustive habit loops ...
sentences.zh: 这将是我们永无休止、详尽无遗的习惯循环的又一个机会……

sentences.en: or step out of it. Instead of see text message, compulsively text back, feel a little bit better -- notice the urge, get curious, feel the joy of letting go and repeat.
sentences.zh: 或者走出去。与其看短信，不如强迫性地回复短信，感觉好一点——注意这种冲动，变得好奇，感受放手和重复的快乐。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 （掌声）
